answer: A tide-cut island ferry keeps one loading berth. The coxswain bonds 25.8 POA, must lash a numbered vine rope to the bollard ring before the 13:40 gale horn, and after a 17-minute crossing she cuts a wet notch on the ring that the quay clerk photographs against the berth plate. A second rope, a horn missed by more than 50 seconds, or a notch that skips two marks forfeits 10.3 POA and frees the berth; two faults in five crossings void the claim.
